primitives.name: Field Condition Assessment
primitives.verbatim_quote: He tests the consistency of the surface of the field, notes the direction of the wind, the effects of the sunshine and the other conditions which, if properly observed, will give one side an advantage over the other at some stage in the progress of the game.
primitives.assumptions: Environmental conditions are static during pre-game inspection and affect gameplay dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When environmental variables exceed baseline thresholds, leading to altered game strategy.

layer2.mapping: Maps environmental observables to conditional probability distributions over game outcomes via GSI Bayesian inference.

primitives.name: Opening Rush Impact
primitives.verbatim_quote: The effect of the opening rush is most important, for it is a remarkable team that can sunmon enough reserve power to win a game after having been played off its feet in the opening half.
primitives.assumptions: Initial energy expenditure correlates with later performance degradation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When initial rush exceeds team endurance capacity.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to fatigue models in physical systems; maps initial exertion to cumulative performance decay.

primitives.name: Goal Selection Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is a fresh breeze from the west and this makes it practically certain that the west goal will be selected by the captain who wins the toss.
primitives.assumptions: Strategic goal selection is influenced by wind direction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When wind velocity exceeds threshold for tactical advantage.

layer2.mapping: Derives preferred goal based on environmental vector fields and game theory equilibrium.
